test_title: SSC Steno 2021 Official Paper (Held on: 15 Nov 2021 Shift 1
subject: general
question: In which year was the first Factory Act passed during colonial rule in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1881**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **committee** appointed in 1875, after inspecting the condition of factories of the passed the first** Factories Act in 1881**.
 
• Following this act, a **Factory Commission** was appointed in 1885.
 
• Then in **1891** another **Factories Act** was adopted.
 
• A **Royal Commission on Labor** was appointed in 1892. 
 
• The main aim of these acts was to **limit the factory working hours**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Factory Act 1891**:

 
 
• Increased the minimum age (**from 7 to 9 years**) & the maximum (**from 12 to 14 years**) for children.
 
• Reduced maximum working hours for children to** 7 hours a day.**
 
• Fixed maximum working hours for women at 11 hours per day with an one &-a-half hour interval.
 
• Provided a weekly holiday for all.
 
• Dangerous machines should be fenced properly to prevent accidents.
 
• Prohibition on employers regarding employing women within 4 weeks after confinement.
 
• This was an answer by the Government to the pathetic conditions of the workers in the factories.
 
• But these laws did not apply to British-owned tea & coffee plantations where the labour was exploited ruthlessly & treated like slaves.
